detailedDerivation: For t<a and d(t)>d(a)=y, y>a>t is nonpast at row t. Coverage and strict row maximum supply one actual interior private y cell. Row injectivity makes its host unique.
Conversely each future-diagonal service y=d(a) at row t has a>t and y<d(t), so it determines exactly that inversion. Injective diagonal labels and row indexes make the correspondence bijective.

For mortal a, p=σ_a satisfies t<a<p<y<d(t), so coverage also supplies a private p cell at row t. This blocker cannot belong to the L cancellation, because its victim a is not yet an old owner. Hence it is B0.

The pair(row t, blocker p) determines the victim a uniquely; distinct mortal inversions thus have distinct target cells. H1 and H2 are distinct copies, not two claims on one positive token. No equality between their different dates is assumed.
